searches.note: Twenty seven searches of a share of twenty eight, one left unspent, none the author's. One search read Magyar Bor and Wines of Hungary together (the Home of Kékfrankos article, shared by Weninger, Luka and Ráspi). The house's own domain was searched only for its own dates, vineyards and methods (pfneiszl.hu, taschner.hu twice, raspi.hu) and blocked where an independent second source was wanted (weninger.com twice, raspi.hu once). No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).
Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was found in no source of this check and rested on the author's reading alone, it was cut or hedged.
Sources whose title or address names a living person were met among the results and are cited neither in the fragment nor here.

tested: The purchase at Balf in 1997: Wine Anorak, Circo Vino, Kensington Wine Market and the house; kept.
The Villány winery of 1992 with a local grower: wein.plus glossary and the Genussland producer page; kept, the partner unnamed.
Gneiss and mica schist, porous, dry and warm: the house, Circo Vino and Magyar Bor (stony schist); kept. One merchant and the plan say grey slate.
Two years in 500 litre barrels: the house's 2018 sheet and In Wines We Trust's 24 months for the 2017; kept as the 2018 sheet.
The son taking Balf on in 2000: Wine Anorak and Schiller Wine; one wiki gives 2002.
Respekt in 2006: refuted; the association was founded in 2007 (BKWine, Meininger) and one account has Weninger join in 2009; the certification of 2006 is in Circo Vino and Williams Corner.
Steiner bottled by Steigler and Luka: Magyar Bor and Wines of Hungary; kept.
The white of the vineyard: sold as Stein Furmint, first vintage 2018 (Drops, Falstaff).

swaps.proposal: Rename Luka's wine from Pinot Noir to Steiner Kékfrankos, house and key kept
swaps.why: No source says the house leads with its Steiner; the Pinot Noir is real and sourced (the house's description through Bortársaság, its grapes through Wines of Hungary), it gives the group a second grape, and a Steiner Kékfrankos would double Weninger's flagship in the same group. The plan keeps Pinot Noir.

tension: The region record's producers line says Ráspi makes sweet wines; no source of this check found one. Reported, not edited.

The plan's why for Weninger speaks of grey slate at the surface; the house and Magyar Bor give gneiss and mica schist (stony schist), one merchant grey slate. The read together agent may wish to align the why.
The author's report asks the plan's why for Taschner to move from 1997 to 1995; Magyar Bor and Wines of Hungary give 1997, the house 1995, so the plan may keep 1997 as Magyar Bor's or name no year.
